class.sofe.necromancer.quote: Death is not the end. It is a contract, and I know how to read the fine print.
class.sofe.sorceress.quote: The stars already wrote your ending. I just read it aloud.
class.sofe.thief.quote: Everything has an owner until I walk by.
class.sofe.king.quote: My ancestor opened this door. I will be the one to close it.

dialogue.sofe.act1.shard.1: The eclipse swallows the sun. Above the Great Observatory, the seal of the Codex cracks like glass.
dialogue.sofe.act1.shard.knight: In the lower district, Cassian steps between a child and a burning shard falling from the sky.
dialogue.sofe.act1.shard.knight.2: It burns... but I am still standing. Run, little one!
dialogue.sofe.act1.shard.necromancer: In the city morgue, Ankhareth is preparing a body when the shard pierces him. The dead man opens his eyes.
dialogue.sofe.act1.shard.necromancer.2: The dead are whispering. They know my name now.
dialogue.sofe.act1.shard.sorceress: In the Great Observatory, Shirin reaches for her astrolabe. The shard falls from the sky straight into her hand.
dialogue.sofe.act1.shard.sorceress.2: The stars are moving... Laleh, is that you?
dialogue.sofe.act1.shard.thief: In the Observatory vault, Rurik closes his fingers around a shard he meant to sell. It fuses with his hand.
dialogue.sofe.act1.shard.thief.2: Let go, let go! ...Well. That is not coming off.
dialogue.sofe.act1.shard.king: On his own throne, before the whole court, the shard pierces Sultan Azhar. The court falls silent.
dialogue.sofe.act1.shard.king.2: Do not kneel. Not now. Something has entered the city.
dialogue.sofe.act1.shard.2: The shard does not kill. It chooses. From the cracks in the sky, the Void pours into the lower district.
dialogue.sofe.act1.shard.ozhan: Bearer! That power will tear you apart unless you learn to hold it. Quickly, before they reach the bazaar.
dialogue.sofe.act1.shard.ozhan.king: My Sultan... the court must not see you like this. Leave the palace in disguise. The Council and I will hold the throne.
dialogue.sofe.act1.shard.hint: Open the skill tree with K and learn your first three skills.
dialogue.sofe.act1.invasion.1: The ground trembles. Shapes without faces crawl out of the shadows of the lower district.
dialogue.sofe.act1.invasion.2: They are here! Use what you have learned, Bearer. Drive them back!
dialogue.sofe.act1.invasion.2.king: They are here, my Sultan. Let your people see a stranger fight for them tonight.
dialogue.sofe.act1.council.1: The Council of Sulthari is gathered, Bearer. Five shards fell tonight, and five of you still breathe.
dialogue.sofe.act1.council.2: I am Azhar, Sultan of Sulthari. A shard pierced me too, on my own throne. We carry the same burden now.
dialogue.sofe.act1.council.1.king: The Council does not know your face tonight, my Sultan. I will speak for the throne while you walk among them.
dialogue.sofe.act1.council.3: The Brass Sentinel of the Great Observatory has woken. It guarded the seal for three hundred years, and now it obeys no one.
dialogue.sofe.act1.council.4.lore: First, tell me about the Codex.
dialogue.sofe.act1.council.4: If the Sentinel falls to the Void, the Observatory falls with it. Will you go?
dialogue.sofe.act1.council.lore: Seven Archsins were sealed in the Codex by the first emperor. Tonight the seal broke in seven places.
dialogue.sofe.act1.council.lore.2: And each shard is a piece of that seal. That is why they chose you. Now, the Sentinel.
dialogue.sofe.act1.epilogue.1: The Brass Sentinel falls silent. Its gears stop, one by one, like a heart that finally rests.
dialogue.sofe.act1.epilogue.2: Sulthari stands, Bearer. But the north burns: Nordrath has fallen to Wrath. The Seal Veil to the north is open for you.
act.sofe.1: Act I: The Night of the Eclipse
act.sofe.4: Act IV: The Republic of Aureum
dialogue.sofe.ozhan.1: The Council watches over Sulthari while you are away, Bearer. Go with the stars.
dialogue.sofe.ozhan.1.king: The throne is safe with me, my Sultan. No one has seen through your disguise.
dialogue.sofe.azhar.1: The operations center is open day and night. Whatever you need to fight the Void, Sulthari will give it.
dialogue.sofe.cassian.1: Keep your guard up. The Void does not tire, and neither can we.
dialogue.sofe.ankhareth.1: The dead of Sulthari are restless tonight. I will keep them in their place.
dialogue.sofe.shirin.1: The constellations have shifted. I have never seen the sky like this.
dialogue.sofe.rurik.1: Don't look at me like that. I was only borrowing the shard.
dialogue.sofe.dilara.1: Brass and steel, Bearer. If it breaks out there, bring it to me.
dialogue.sofe.dilara.embers.1: The Void is still crawling out near the Low Bazaar. The guards cannot hold both the bazaar and the Observatory.
dialogue.sofe.dilara.embers.2: The Council elder is at the Observatory deciding where to send them. Talk to him. Please.
dialogue.sofe.council_elder.1: The Observatory has watched the seal for three centuries. It will not stop watching now.
dialogue.sofe.council_elder.embers.1: I have guards for one place, not two. The Low Bazaar feeds the city. The Observatory keeps what is left of the seal.
dialogue.sofe.council_elder.embers.bazaa: Protect the Low Bazaar. The people come first.
dialogue.sofe.council_elder.embers.obser: Protect the Observatory. Without the seal there is no city.
dialogue.sofe.council_elder.embers.2: You are a Bearer. You choose, and I will send the others where you do not stand.
dialogue.sofe.ferid.1: Potions, flasks, herbs. Everything a Bearer needs to stay alive a little longer.
dialogue.sofe.yusuf.1: Torches, arrows, bread and a Return Scroll for when the road goes wrong.
dialogue.sofe.selim.1: Emeralds for Dinars, Dinars for emeralds. Honest rates, mostly.

dialogue.sofe.act1.festival.1: Sulthari, the last free city of Aetheris. Tonight is the Eclipse Festival.
dialogue.sofe.act1.festival.2: Brass tramways ring through the markets. Lanterns of aetherium float above the domes, and the Great Observatory shines like a second moon.
dialogue.sofe.act1.festival.3: Three hundred years ago, seven sins were sealed in the Codex. Tonight, as the moon covers the sun, five strangers will learn why.
dialogue.sofe.act1.festival.4: One of them is you. Who are you, Bearer?
dialogue.sofe.act1.sentinel.1: The Sentinel is in the Great Observatory. Its gears were made to guard the seal; now the Void turns them.
dialogue.sofe.act1.sentinel.2: Break it before the Void finishes the work. Bring your strongest skills.

quest.sofe.act2_north.step4: Face Vorath, Archsin of Wrath, at the Burning Citadel.
dialogue.sofe.act2.north.1: The Veil to the north has opened for you. Beyond it, the clans of Nordrath fight a war that never ends.
dialogue.sofe.act2.north.2: Vorath raises their dead every dawn so they can kill each other again. Two of his oath-breakers guard the way: Kaleth at the Forge, Serath at the Arena.
dialogue.sofe.act2.north.3: Break them, and the gates of the Burning Citadel will open.
dialogue.sofe.act2.citadel.1: The Burning Citadel stands on black rock. Its walls are warm to the touch, as if something inside never stopped breathing fire.
dialogue.sofe.act2.citadel.2: Kaleth and Serath are gone. The gate is open.
dialogue.sofe.act2.vorath.1: Another Bearer. Another shard. You came all this way to make me stop?
dialogue.sofe.act2.vorath.knight: Knight of the Scale. I know you. Your order died protecting cowards who sold them. Take my strength. Stop protecting. Only destroy, and no one will betray you again.
dialogue.sofe.act2.vorath.other: I can feel your anger, Bearer. Everyone has it. Let it out, and I will make you strong enough to burn the whole Void.
dialogue.sofe.act2.vorath.2: Fight me, and your anger is mine anyway.
dialogue.sofe.act2.thank_you.1: Vorath falls. Across Nordrath, the warriors of the endless war lower their weapons and, at last, lie still.
dialogue.sofe.act2.thank_you.2: His Codex Shard rises from the ashes. For a moment it is cold, and a voice that is not Vorath's speaks through it.
dialogue.sofe.act2.thank_you.4: Beneath the Citadel, the crack Vorath kept closed glows red. The Burning Deep is open.
dialogue.sofe.ozhan.act2.1: The north burns, Bearer. Kaleth guards the Forge and Serath the Arena; only then will the Citadel open.

dialogue.sofe.citizen_baker.act1.1: The festival bread was still warm when the sky went dark. Now I bake for the guards on the walls.
dialogue.sofe.citizen_baker.act1.2: Eat something, Bearer. Even a hero walks on bread before walking on legends.
dialogue.sofe.citizen_baker.act2.1: No ships come from the north anymore. They say the Norse dead rise every dawn to fight again.
dialogue.sofe.citizen_baker.act2.2: If you go to Nordrath, take warm bread. The cold there bites like a moneylender.
dialogue.sofe.citizen_baker.act3.1: The bells rang all night when word came that Vorath had fallen. My ovens have never been so busy!
dialogue.sofe.citizen_baker.act3.2: Still... a fragment that thanks you is no gift. My grandmother said: never trust bread that bakes itself.
dialogue.sofe.citizen_water_carrier.act1: The fountains of the plaza run on aetherium pumps. On the night of the eclipse they ran black for an hour.
I still dream of that water. It whispered.
dialogue.sofe.citizen_water_carrier.act2: The wells of the lower district are clean again, thanks to you Bearers. But the Void creatures still crawl beyond the walls at night.
dialogue.sofe.citizen_water_carrier.act3: The water has tasted of iron since the crack opened. The Observatory says it is nothing. The Observatory said that before, too.
dialogue.sofe.citizen_scholar.act1.1: A thousand years ago five emperors read five pages of a book they should have burned. We call it the Ritual of the Five Crowns.
dialogue.sofe.citizen_scholar.act1.2: The Observatory keeps the oldest records. Ask the Council Elder if you want the whole story.
dialogue.sofe.citizen_scholar.act2.1: Seven fragments of the First Fallen escaped the crack: the Seven Archsins. Wrath went north, to Nordrath.
dialogue.sofe.citizen_scholar.act2.2: Each Archsin twisted the guardians of the Ten Laws. Those who broke their law became the Broken Oaths.
dialogue.sofe.citizen_scholar.act3.1: Lust holds Parsivan and Sloth holds Khemet. Two empires asleep: one in pleasure, one in death.
dialogue.sofe.citizen_scholar.act3.2: If you find anything written by the sultan who sealed the crack, bring it to me. Please.
dialogue.sofe.citizen_guard.act1.1: Stay inside the walls after dark, traveler. The aetherium barrier kept us safe for a thousand years, and now it hums like a wasp.
dialogue.sofe.citizen_guard.act1.2: We drill with the clockwork spears every morning. Much good they did against the Sentinel.
dialogue.sofe.citizen_guard.act2.1: The gates are open again since the Sentinel fell. I count every caravan that leaves. Fewer come back.
dialogue.sofe.citizen_guard.act3.1: The patrols saw the smoke in the north go out. Whatever you did in Nordrath, the night watch is quieter.
dialogue.sofe.citizen_weaver.act1.1: My carpets tell the story of the Pact: five crowns, ten laws, one table. I leave a sixth chair empty in every one. Grandmother's custom.
dialogue.sofe.citizen_weaver.act2.1: Red thread is dear now. Everyone wants banners for the walls.
dialogue.sofe.citizen_weaver.act3.1: A merchant from the east sold me silk that never frays. Beautiful... and it smelled of sleep. I burned it.
dialogue.sofe.citizen_pilgrim.act1.1: I walked from the outer oases to watch the eclipse from the Observatory. I watched the sky tear instead.
dialogue.sofe.citizen_pilgrim.act2.1: The road north is lined with the cairns of the Norse clans. They bury their dead, and the dead do not stay buried.
dialogue.sofe.citizen_pilgrim.act3.1: I will go east next, to Khemet's river. They say the living there no longer move. Maybe they are only praying.
dialogue.sofe.citizen_widow.act1.1: My husband kept the brass gears of the Observatory clean. He was inside when the seal broke.
dialogue.sofe.citizen_widow.act1.2: Do not look at me like that. Find who did this.
dialogue.sofe.citizen_widow.act2.1: They say the Broken Oaths were guardians once, sworn to the Laws. My husband swore oaths too. Men are fragile things.
dialogue.sofe.citizen_widow.act3.1: You came back from the north alive. Good. Keep doing that.
dialogue.sofe.citizen_clockmaker.act1.1: The Brass Sentinel was my master's work. A guardian of the city... and the crack turned it against us.
dialogue.sofe.citizen_clockmaker.act1.2: Aetherium is like a heart. When it turns black, everything it moves goes mad.
dialogue.sofe.citizen_clockmaker.act2.1: I salvaged a gear from the Sentinel. It still turns by itself at night. I keep it in a jar.
dialogue.sofe.citizen_clockmaker.act3.1: Black aetherium from the Archsins' lands can be purified. The forge masters know how; listen to them.
dialogue.sofe.citizen_child.act1.1: Are you a Bearer? Does the shard hurt? Can I touch it? ...No? Okay.
dialogue.sofe.citizen_child.act2.1: I play Bearers and Archsins with my friends. I'm always Vorath. He's the loudest.
dialogue.sofe.citizen_child.act3.1: Mama says you beat Vorath! I'll play someone else now. Maybe you!
dialogue.sofe.citizen_storyteller.ask: Gather round, gather round! A meddah never tells the same tale twice... unless you pay him. What shall I tell you?
The Pact of the Five Crowns
dialogue.sofe.citizen_storyteller.tale.1: Five empires, ten laws, one table: Sulthari of brass, Nordrath of the axe, Parsivan of the gardens, Khemet of the river and Aureum of marble. For a thousand years the Pact held...
dialogue.sofe.citizen_storyteller.tale.2: ...until the emperors found a book beneath our desert. Each read one page aloud. Seven shadows came out of the crack, and our sultan gave his life to close it beneath the Observatory.
dialogue.sofe.citizen_storyteller.tale.3: On the Night of the Eclipse five shards found five hearts. Some say they are heroes. Some say the Codex chose its own messengers. I say: buy a cup of tea and decide for yourself.
dialogue.sofe.citizen_storyteller.tale.4: Ten guardians kept the Ten Laws. The Archsins whispered to each one, and each broke the law they kept. Now they fight with the very sin they swore to stop.
dialogue.sofe.bazaar_spicer.act1.1: Saffron, sumac, mountain sage! Everything the Alembic needs, and half of what a good soup needs.
dialogue.sofe.bazaar_spicer.act2.1: Herbs from the north freeze on the road. Grow your own, Bearer: plant pomegranates where the sun is kind.
dialogue.sofe.bazaar_weaver.act1.1: Wool from the plateau herds, dyed in the colors of the Dominion. Red for courage, gold for the sultan.
dialogue.sofe.bazaar_weaver.act2.1: Everyone wants banners now. Even the bakers hang a crescent over their ovens.
dialogue.sofe.bazaar_fruiterer.act1.1: Figs, apples and the best pomegranates south of the walls. A Bearer must eat!
dialogue.sofe.bazaar_fruiterer.act2.1: The caravans from the north are back. Prices are falling, and so is my mood.
dialogue.sofe.bazaar_lampwright.act1.1: Aetherium lamps, brass lanterns, glass blown here in Sulthari. Darkness is bad for business, Bearer.
dialogue.sofe.bazaar_lampwright.act2.1: Since the crack opened, everyone buys a second lamp. I am not complaining.
dialogue.sofe.citizen_tram_keeper.act1.1: The brass tramways ran all night for the festival. Then the Sentinel tore the rails out with its bare hands.
dialogue.sofe.citizen_tram_keeper.act1.2: We will lay them again. Sulthari always rebuilds.
dialogue.sofe.citizen_tram_keeper.act2.1: The first line runs again, from the plaza to the bazaar. Slowly. The gears remember the night of the eclipse.
dialogue.sofe.citizen_tram_keeper.act3.1: The Council wants a line to the gates, for the caravans. Victories are good for business, Bearer.
dialogue.sofe.citizen_fisherman.act1.1: From the cliffs you can see the whole bay. On the night of the eclipse the fish all swam away from the city at once.
dialogue.sofe.citizen_fisherman.act2.1: The causeways to the gates are safe again. The fish are not back yet. Fish are wiser than people.
dialogue.sofe.citizen_fisherman.act3.1: The fish came back the week Vorath fell. My wife says it is a sign. I say it is dinner.
dialogue.sofe.citizen_veteran.act1.1: Forty years on these walls and I never drew my sword in anger. Then the Void came up from below, not over the walls.
dialogue.sofe.citizen_veteran.act2.1: A guardian who breaks his oath is worse than any monster. A monster never promised you anything.
dialogue.sofe.citizen_veteran.act3.1: You fought Wrath and kept your head. Good. Wrath is the easiest sin to see. The others hide better.
dialogue.sofe.citizen_courier.act1.1: Letters for the Council, letters for the forge, letters for everyone who is still alive. Busy night, Bearer.
dialogue.sofe.citizen_courier.act2.1: No courier comes back from Nordrath. So now I carry letters to the north gate and leave them there. Silly, I know.
dialogue.sofe.citizen_courier.act3.1: A letter arrived from Nordrath! Signed by a clan chief. It only says: 'We sleep now. Thank the Bearer.'
dialogue.sofe.citizen_astronomer.act1.1: The eclipse was predicted to the minute. What nobody predicted was the seal breaking under the Great Lens.
dialogue.sofe.citizen_astronomer.act2.1: Seven new lights appeared in the northern sky the night of the eclipse. One of them went out. I think you did that.
dialogue.sofe.citizen_astronomer.act3.1: Six lights left. One burns over Parsivan, one over Khemet. The brightest stands right above us, and it never moves.
dialogue.sofe.citizen_tea_seller.act1.1: Tea calms the nerves, Bearer. And after last night, the whole city needs a cup.
dialogue.sofe.citizen_tea_seller.act2.1: People talk over tea. They say the Grand Vizier never sleeps. They say he did not even blink when the seal broke.
dialogue.sofe.citizen_tea_seller.act3.1: More gossip? The Grand Vizier ordered new locks for the Observatory. Locks, Bearer. What is he keeping in?

dialogue.sofe.nordrath_shieldmaiden.act1: I died on the ice yesterday. And the day before. Every dawn Vorath's fire wakes us and the war starts again.
You do not wake with us, Bearer. That means you can end it.
dialogue.sofe.nordrath_shieldmaiden.act3: This morning I woke and nobody called me to the shieldwall. I did not know what to do with my hands.
dialogue.sofe.nordrath_fisher.act1.1: The fjord does not freeze anymore. The mountain keeps it warm, and the fish taste of ash.
dialogue.sofe.nordrath_fisher.act3.1: The water is cold again! Cold and clean. I never thought I would be glad to lose a finger to the ice.
dialogue.sofe.nordrath_widow.act1.1: My husband falls every evening and stands up every morning. I have buried him a hundred times. Do not ask me to cry again.
dialogue.sofe.nordrath_widow.act3.1: He did not wake today. I sat by him until noon. Then I laughed, Bearer, because he looked rested.
dialogue.sofe.nordrath_apprentice.act1.1: The forges here drink lava straight from the mountain. Master says Kaleth taught the first smiths before he broke his oath.
dialogue.sofe.nordrath_apprentice.act3.1: The lava runs slower since Vorath fell. Master says the mountain is sleeping. I say it is listening.
dialogue.sofe.nordrath_hunter.act1.1: Wolves stay away from the hold. Even beasts know the dead here do not stay dead.
dialogue.sofe.nordrath_hunter.act3.1: The wolves came back to the forest last night. I have never been so happy to hear them howl.
dialogue.sofe.nordrath_elder.act1.1: The Pact gave us the Law of the winter bread, and Kaleth the Law of mercy. Now Kaleth burns those who kneel.
dialogue.sofe.nordrath_elder.act3.1: Something sleeps under the Caverns, Bearer. It is hungry. When the time comes, do not go down there with an empty stomach.
dialogue.sofe.nordrath_child.act1.1: Papa says when I grow up I will fight forever too. I do not want to fight forever.
dialogue.sofe.nordrath_child.act3.1: Now I can grow up and be a fisher instead! Or a dragon. A small one.
dialogue.sofe.nordrath_brewer.act1.1: Mead does not help the dead, but it helps the living watch them march out again.
dialogue.sofe.nordrath_brewer.act3.1: A feast! The first in a hundred years without a war the next morning. Drink, Bearer, you paid for it.
dialogue.sofe.nordrath_raider.act1.1: I sailed to Aureum once, when there were still ships worth robbing. Now the only plunder left is our own graves.
dialogue.sofe.nordrath_raider.act3.1: Serath honoured no blood but her own. Thank you for showing her the old law, Bearer.
dialogue.sofe.nordrath_skald.ask: Sit by the fire, stranger. A skald pays for his mead with sagas. Which one will you hear?
dialogue.sofe.nordrath_skald.tale.1: Nine clans signed the Pact for Nordrath: the axe and the oar, the forge and the fjord. We kept the Laws of mercy and of the winter bread longer than any.
dialogue.sofe.nordrath_skald.tale.2: When Wrath came out of the crack, it found the bravest warriors of Aetheris. Vorath gave them what they wanted most: a battle that never ends. Every dawn, his fire raises the fallen.
dialogue.sofe.nordrath_skald.tale.3: Kaleth guarded the Law of mercy and now finishes the fallen in his Forge. Serath guarded the blood of our fathers and now drinks it in her Arena. Both serve Vorath in the Burning Citadel.
dialogue.sofe.nordrath_skald.tale.4: Our forges burn with a fire that comes from below. The old ones say there is a deep beneath the deep, and that it opens only when Wrath is silenced.
dialogue.sofe.nordrath_furrier.act1.1: Furs, smoked fish and mead. Nothing keeps a Bearer alive in the north like a good cloak.
dialogue.sofe.nordrath_furrier.act3.1: Business is good since the dead stopped buying. They never paid anyway.
dialogue.sofe.nordrath_runesmith.act1.1: Glacial iron, forged in volcano fire and quenched in the fjord. Nothing else holds an edge in this cold.
dialogue.sofe.nordrath_runesmith.act3.1: Vorath's fall cooled the mountain a little. My forge will miss him. I will not.

quest.sofe.bearer.cassian_act1.step2: Go back to whoever asked for your help in Sulthari.
dialogue.sofe.q.cassian_act1.offer.1: You carry a banner nobody in Sulthari recognises, Knight. I fought beside men who carried it, long ago.
dialogue.sofe.q.cassian_act1.offer.2: The Void is gnawing at the lower district. Show me the Order of the Scale still stands, and I will tell you what I saw the night it fell.
dialogue.sofe.q.cassian_act1.reminder: The Void is still in the lower district. The Scale does not hide.
dialogue.sofe.q.cassian_act1.done.1: You fought like them. Like the ones who did not betray you.
dialogue.sofe.q.cassian_act1.done.2: Your brothers did not fall to the Void. Gold opened the gates of the courts, gold from Aureum. Take this charm; it was your captain's.
quest.sofe.bearer.cassian_act2.step3: Go back to whoever asked for your help in Skarnhold.
dialogue.sofe.q.cassian_act2.offer.1: Southerner. Vorath's voice speaks of you in the arena. He says your wrath is the sweetest he has smelled.
dialogue.sofe.q.cassian_act2.offer.2: Go there and fight, but fight to protect. If you fight to destroy, he wins without lifting a hand.
dialogue.sofe.q.cassian_act2.accept: I fight for whoever stands behind me.
dialogue.sofe.q.cassian_act2.reminder: The arena waits, east of the hold. Remember why you lift the shield.
dialogue.sofe.q.cassian_act2.done.1: The warriors say you held the line and did not chase the ones who fled.
dialogue.sofe.q.cassian_act2.done.2: That is the Scale I have heard of. Take this blade; my clan forged it for a knight who never came.
quest.sofe.bearer.ankhareth_act1.step2: Go back to whoever asked for your help in Sulthari.
dialogue.sofe.q.ankhareth_act1.offer.1: You work in the morgue, embalmer. My husband lies there. Since the Eclipse he will not stay still.
dialogue.sofe.q.ankhareth_act1.offer.2: The Void creatures are drawn to him. Drive them off, and give him the rest your people promised.
dialogue.sofe.q.ankhareth_act1.accept: The House of Thresholds keeps its word.
dialogue.sofe.q.ankhareth_act1.reminder: They still come for him at night. Please.
dialogue.sofe.q.ankhareth_act1.done.1: He is still. For the first time since the Eclipse, he is still.
dialogue.sofe.q.ankhareth_act1.done.2: He kept this scarab for you. He said the embalmer would need it more than the dead.
quest.sofe.bearer.ankhareth_act2.step3: Go back to whoever asked for your help in Skarnhold.
dialogue.sofe.q.ankhareth_act2.offer.1: Our dead do not go to the halls of their fathers anymore, priest of Khemet. They wander the caverns to the west.
dialogue.sofe.q.ankhareth_act2.offer.2: Something holds them there. You know the roads of the dead. Open the way.
dialogue.sofe.q.ankhareth_act2.reminder: The caverns are west of the hold. Our dead are waiting.
dialogue.sofe.q.ankhareth_act2.done.1: The fires in the hall burned blue last night. The old ones say that is how the dead say farewell.
dialogue.sofe.q.ankhareth_act2.done.2: This wand was found in the caverns, older than our clans. It belongs to someone who guides the dead.
quest.sofe.bearer.shirin_act1.step2: Go back to whoever asked for your help in Sulthari.
dialogue.sofe.q.shirin_act1.offer.1: Shirin! Letters keep arriving at the Observatory in your sister's hand, but they are dated after Parsivan fell.
dialogue.sofe.q.shirin_act1.offer.2: The Void gathers wherever the letters land. Clear them, and read what she wrote.
dialogue.sofe.q.shirin_act1.accept: If she is writing, she is still there.
dialogue.sofe.q.shirin_act1.reminder: The creatures still circle the letters. Be careful.
dialogue.sofe.q.shirin_act1.done.1: The last letter says only: 'Stay with me in the garden, little star.'
dialogue.sofe.q.shirin_act1.done.2: It was wrapped around this charm. It is warm, like an ember that never went out.
quest.sofe.bearer.shirin_act2.step3: Go back to whoever asked for your help in Skarnhold.
dialogue.sofe.q.shirin_act2.offer.1: A woman of the south came through the snow before the war, lady. She left a lantern at the forge and said a sister would come for it.
dialogue.sofe.q.shirin_act2.offer.2: Kaleth's creatures guard the forge now.
dialogue.sofe.q.shirin_act2.reminder: The forge is west, past the frozen river.
dialogue.sofe.q.shirin_act2.done.1: You found it. It still burns, after all this time.
dialogue.sofe.q.shirin_act2.done.2: She said whoever carried it would never lose her way in the dark.
quest.sofe.bearer.rurik_act1.step2: Go back to whoever asked for your help in Sulthari.
dialogue.sofe.q.rurik_act1.offer.1: Ash! The buyer for that shard is still waiting. The one stuck in your hand, yes.
dialogue.sofe.q.rurik_act1.offer.2: He won't pay for a hand. But the Void things in the bazaar scare my customers. Clear them and I'll pay you like old times.
dialogue.sofe.q.rurik_act1.reminder: They're still scaring off my customers, Ash.
dialogue.sofe.q.rurik_act1.done.1: Here's your pay. And something else: a man asked about you. A northerner, with a burned clan mark.
dialogue.sofe.q.rurik_act1.done.2: He said the fire that took your village was no accident. He said a name: Fenrath.
quest.sofe.bearer.rurik_act2.step3: Go back to whoever asked for your help in Skarnhold.
dialogue.sofe.q.rurik_act2.offer.1: Grimsson. I thought your clan burned to the last child.
dialogue.sofe.q.rurik_act2.offer.2: The raiders who did it hid their spoils in the western caverns. Some of it was yours.
dialogue.sofe.q.rurik_act2.reminder: West caverns. Take back what is yours.
dialogue.sofe.q.rurik_act2.done.1: There it is: your father's knife, and a ledger with one name written in ash. Fenrath.
dialogue.sofe.q.rurik_act2.done.2: Whatever you do with that name, Grimsson, do it awake.
quest.sofe.bearer.azhar_act1.step2: Go back to whoever asked for your help in Sulthari.
dialogue.sofe.q.azhar_act1.offer.1: Your Majesty! The people say the Sultan hides in the palace while the Void walks the streets.
dialogue.sofe.q.azhar_act1.offer.2: If they saw you fight beside the guard, they would believe again.
dialogue.sofe.q.azhar_act1.done.1: They cheered, Majesty. Even the old ones who cursed your grandfather.
dialogue.sofe.q.azhar_act1.done.2: The mint struck this coin for the day of your crowning. It was never given out. It is yours.
quest.sofe.bearer.azhar_act2.step3: Go back to whoever asked for your help in Skarnhold.
dialogue.sofe.q.azhar_act2.offer.1: A sultan in the snow. The clans won't kneel to you, southerner.
dialogue.sofe.q.azhar_act2.offer.2: But they respect deeds. Free the forge from Kaleth's beasts, and they will listen to what Sulthari wants.
dialogue.sofe.q.azhar_act2.reminder: The forge, west. Deeds, not words.
dialogue.sofe.q.azhar_act2.done.1: The clans saw. They say a sultan who bleeds for others is a sultan they could follow.
dialogue.sofe.q.azhar_act2.done.2: This scepter came north with the first sultan's envoy, three hundred years ago. It goes back with you.
quest.sofe.side.nordrath_endless_war.ste: Go back to whoever asked for your help in Skarnhold.
dialogue.sofe.q.nordrath_endless_war.off: Hear the saga no skald wants to sing: the warriors who fell in Vorath's arena do not stay dead. They rise and fight again, forever.
Go to the arena. Break the ones who rise. Then come back, and decide how the saga ends.
dialogue.sofe.q.nordrath_endless_war.rem: The arena, east of the hold. The dead are still fighting.
dialogue.sofe.q.nordrath_endless_war.cho: You broke them, and they rose again. Only the ones who set the war can end it. You carry a shard of what set it.
Will you free them, and let the clans mourn and make peace? Or let them fight forever, so the clans stay fierce for the wars to come?
dialogue.sofe.q.nordrath_endless_war.ans: Free them. Let the clans mourn.
dialogue.sofe.q.nordrath_endless_war.rep: Then the saga ends in silence. A good silence.
dialogue.sofe.q.nordrath_endless_war.ans: Let them fight. The north will need warriors.
dialogue.sofe.q.nordrath_endless_war.rep: Then the saga never ends. The clans will remember your choice.
quest.sofe.side.nordrath_cold_forge.step: Go back to whoever asked for your help in Skarnhold.
dialogue.sofe.q.nordrath_cold_forge.offe: The great forge of the north went cold when Kaleth took it. Without it, no glacial iron for the clans.
His beasts still guard the anvils. Clear them, and I'll light it again.
dialogue.sofe.q.nordrath_cold_forge.remi: The forge, west of the hold.
dialogue.sofe.q.nordrath_cold_forge.done: The forge burns again! The first ingots are yours.
Whatever the clans decide about the war, they'll fight it with good steel now.
dialogue.sofe.cassian.act1: The shard chose me because I stepped in front of a child. I would do it again.
dialogue.sofe.cassian.act2: Vorath whispers that I could end all of this with enough rage. He is right. That is what frightens me.
companion.sofe.knight.dismissed: I'll be in Sulthari, by the palace. Call if you need a wall.
companion.sofe.knight.down: I... must fall back. To Sulthari.
companion.sofe.knight.boss: One less voice in the dark.
companion.sofe.knight.region.nordrath: I can feel Vorath's rage in the air. Keep me from it.
companion.sofe.knight.region.parsivan: Flowers that smell of sleep. Stay awake.
companion.sofe.knight.region.khemet: The dead here are too quiet.
companion.sofe.knight.region.aureum: Aureum. The courts where my order died. Let me pass judgment.
dialogue.sofe.ankhareth.act1: The dead in this city are restless. I hear them at night, asking which way to go.
dialogue.sofe.ankhareth.act2: Sometimes I think it would be easy to lie down beside them and sleep. Morthis would like that.
companion.sofe.necromancer.hired: The dead will walk beside us. Do not be afraid of them.
companion.sofe.necromancer.dismissed: I return to the morgue. Someone has to listen to them.
companion.sofe.necromancer.down: My thread is cut... for now.
companion.sofe.necromancer.boss: Its soul goes where it must.
companion.sofe.necromancer.region.nordra: The northern dead want to fight even after death.
companion.sofe.necromancer.region.parsiv: The dreamers here are neither dead nor alive.
companion.sofe.necromancer.region.khemet: Khemet. My home. Morthis will try to make me sleep. Do not let me.
companion.sofe.necromancer.region.aureum: So much gold, and the dead still unpaid.
dialogue.sofe.shirin.act1: Laleh taught me to read the stars. Now they read me back.
dialogue.sofe.shirin.act2: In my dreams the gardens are warm and she is laughing. I wake up colder every time.
companion.sofe.sorceress.hired: The stars say we'll go far together.
companion.sofe.sorceress.dismissed: I'll be at the Observatory, reading the sky for you.
companion.sofe.sorceress.boss: Write that one down in the stars.
companion.sofe.sorceress.region.nordrath: Too cold for poetry. Not too cold for fire.
companion.sofe.sorceress.region.parsivan: Parsivan... I can hear her. Laleh is calling. Hold my hand.
companion.sofe.sorceress.region.khemet: The stars here are older than the sand.
companion.sofe.sorceress.region.aureum: Marble and lies. Watch your back.
dialogue.sofe.rurik.act1: Somebody's paying good money for this shard. Shame it's stuck to my hand.
dialogue.sofe.rurik.act2: The north smells like my village did. Before the fire.
companion.sofe.thief.dismissed: I'll be in the Low Bazaar. Don't let anyone sell you fake relics.
companion.sofe.thief.down: Ugh. I'm out. See you at the bazaar.
companion.sofe.thief.region.sulthari: Sulthari. Smell of spice and debts.
companion.sofe.thief.region.nordrath: Home. Or what's left of it.
companion.sofe.thief.region.parsivan: Pretty place. Too pretty. Check your pockets.
companion.sofe.thief.region.khemet: Tombs full of gold, and nobody guarding them? That's a trap.
companion.sofe.thief.region.aureum: Avarok's vaults are here. Don't let me near them.
dialogue.sofe.azhar.act1: My ancestor opened this door. The least I can do is help close it.
dialogue.sofe.azhar.act2: The clans respect strength, not crowns. I am learning which one I have.
companion.sofe.king.dismissed: I return to the palace. The Council will want a report.
companion.sofe.king.down: Even sultans must retreat. To the palace.
companion.sofe.king.boss: Let them write it in the chronicles.
companion.sofe.king.region.sulthari: My city. My people. My debt.
companion.sofe.king.region.nordrath: The clans watch me like a wolf watches a lamb. Let them.
companion.sofe.king.region.parsivan: Parsivan's court once sent us roses every spring.
companion.sofe.king.region.khemet: My grandfather's diary spoke of Khemet. Little of it was kind.
companion.sofe.king.region.aureum: Aureum. Where emperors forget they are men. Remind me, if I do.
dialogue.sofe.nordrath_skald.fate.peace: The warriors of the arena rest. The clans sang for them three nights. I sang the loudest.
dialogue.sofe.nordrath_skald.fate.war: Hear them? Steel on steel, every night, from the arena. The young ones go to watch, and come back hungry for war.

message.sofe.fenrath.swallowed: Fenrath swallows you! Your allies must strike him
message.sofe.luxara.charmed: Charmed: you walk to her, and cannot raise a hand against your own
message.sofe.luxara.mirrors: Luxara's mirrors rise: blows come back
message.sofe.morthis.risen: The marsh gives up its dead for Morthis
message.sofe.avarok.returned: What Avarok stole is yours again
message.sofe.gularth.devours: Gularth devours the floor beneath you!
dialogue.sofe.luxara.1: You came so far, Bearer, and still you ache. I know that ache. In my gardens no one is ever alone again.
dialogue.sofe.luxara.own: Shirin. Laleh is here. Listen: she is humming the song from the observatory roof. Stay, and you will never lose her a second time.
dialogue.sofe.luxara.other: Whatever you lost, it waits among the flowers. Every face you miss, every hand you let go.
dialogue.sofe.luxara.2: Give me the shard, and the dream is yours forever.
dialogue.sofe.luxara.refuse: No. A dream you cannot wake from is a cage.
dialogue.sofe.morthis.1: Shhh. Why do you hurry? The river does not hurry. The dead do not hurry. Only the living tire themselves, and for what?
dialogue.sofe.morthis.own: Ankhareth, priest of thresholds. Your master sleeps here, beside the others. Lie down with them. No more pain, no more doors to open. Rest.
dialogue.sofe.morthis.other: Rest, Bearer. Set down the shard; it is so heavy. Let Khemet keep you, as it keeps everyone.
dialogue.sofe.morthis.2: Close your eyes. Only for a moment.
dialogue.sofe.morthis.refuse: I will rest when the dead can.
dialogue.sofe.avarok.1: Welcome to the Vaults. Every coin of Aureum came to me in the end. Every one. And you, Bearer, what do you carry? Show me.
dialogue.sofe.avarok.own: Rurik Grimsson. Little thief of the north. More gold than all the clans of Nordrath have ever seen. Walk out with it. All of it. Only leave the others behind.
dialogue.sofe.avarok.other: Name your price. Everyone has one. Hand me the shard and I will fill your arms with gold until you cannot lift them.
dialogue.sofe.avarok.2: Well? A merchant's offer does not wait forever.
dialogue.sofe.avarok.refuse: Keep your gold. It has already bought too much.
dialogue.sofe.gularth.1: Hungry. Always hungry. The clans shared their winter bread once, and I ate it. And the clans. And the winter.
dialogue.sofe.gularth.other: You smell of long roads and empty bellies. Sit. Eat. There is always more at my table.
dialogue.sofe.gularth.2: Feed me the shard, Bearer, and you will never know hunger again.
dialogue.sofe.gularth.refuse: Your feast is a grave with a tablecloth.
dialogue.sofe.envyris.1: Look at you. Chosen by the Codex. Everyone in Sulthari speaks your name.
dialogue.sofe.envyris.other: I want it. Your name, your face, your story. I will wear them better than you ever did.
dialogue.sofe.envyris.2: Give me the shard, and I will give you back a life no one notices. Isn't that a kind of peace?
dialogue.sofe.envyris.refuse: You can copy my steps, never the reason I walk.

quest.sofe.act3_east.step3: Defeat Thessyn on the Silk Road
quest.sofe.act3_east.step4: Defeat Luxara in the Enchanted Gardens
quest.sofe.act3_east.step6: Defeat Dormiel in the Khemet Catacombs
quest.sofe.act3_east.step7: Defeat Morthis in the Stagnant Marsh
quest.sofe.act4_west.step4: Defeat Avarok in the Golden Vaults
quest.sofe.act4_west.step5: Defeat Fenrath in the Nordrath Caverns
quest.sofe.act4_west.step6: Defeat Gularth in the Feast Halls
quest.sofe.act4_west.step8: Defeat Envyris on the Shadow Throne
dialogue.sofe.act3.the_eastern_shadows.1: East of Sulthari the roads grow soft with petals. Parsivan was the court of poets; now it is a paradise where no one wants to wake.
dialogue.sofe.act3.the_eastern_shadows.2: Two Broken Oaths guard Luxara: Mirael in the old baths and Thessyn on the Silk Road. Break them, and her gardens will open to you.
dialogue.sofe.act3.the_eastern_shadows.3: Beyond Parsivan lies Khemet, where the dead stopped departing. Its catacombs stay sealed until Luxara falls.
dialogue.sofe.act3.the_gardens.1: The gates of the Enchanted Gardens open without a sound. The air smells of rosewater, and somewhere a woman is singing.
dialogue.sofe.act3.the_gardens.2: Every path leads to the fountain at the heart. Every path wants you to stay.
dialogue.sofe.act3.laleh_at_rest.1: When Luxara falls, the singing stops. For a moment the gardens are only gardens: tired roses, cracked tiles, a fountain that needs cleaning.
dialogue.sofe.act3.laleh_at_rest.2: Her Codex Shard is warm. Too warm. Far to the south, the seal on the Catacombs of Khemet breaks.
dialogue.sofe.act3.the_marsh.1: The river of Khemet does not flow here. It lies still under a green skin, and the pyramid in the middle of it is sinking, slowly, as if it had all the time in the world.
dialogue.sofe.act3.the_marsh.2: On its terrace something enormous sits on a throne. It has not stood up in a thousand years. It does not intend to start now.
dialogue.sofe.act3.the_sultans_diary.1: Among the reeds of Morthis's terrace lies a satchel sealed with the crescent of Sulthari. Inside, a diary in the hand of the last sultan, the one who closed the crack.
dialogue.sofe.act3.the_sultans_diary.2: "They cannot take the fragments. They tried, and the Codex burned them. A fragment must be given, willingly, by the hand that carries it."
dialogue.sofe.act3.the_sultans_diary.3: "That is why they tempt. That is why they will always tempt. Whoever finds this: do not give them what they ask for. Not even once."
dialogue.sofe.act3.the_sultans_diary.4: A diary? Bring it to me, Bearer, the Council must study it. And make haste west: Aureum and its vaults await you.
dialogue.sofe.act4.the_western_ruins.1: Aureum was a republic of marble and law. Now its forum is a market of souls, and in its colosseum the dead fight for coins they cannot spend.
dialogue.sofe.act4.the_western_ruins.2: Avarok sits on the Golden Vaults, behind Goldarc in the Treasury and Nixara in the Market. Envyris rules the ruined senate, the Shadow Throne.
dialogue.sofe.act4.the_western_ruins.3: And under Nordrath, in the caverns, Gularth eats. The Caverns are open to you now.
dialogue.sofe.act4.below_the_north.1: The stair under Skarnhold goes down and down. The air turns warm and sour; somewhere below, something is chewing.
dialogue.sofe.act4.the_shadow_throne.1: The senate of Aureum has no roof. Black mirrors stand where the senators' statues were, and in each of them you see yourself, a little better than you are.
dialogue.sofe.act4.sulthari_besieged.1: Envyris's shard falls into your hand, and with it a silence so deep you can hear your own heart.
dialogue.sofe.act4.sulthari_besieged.2: Then a messenger hawk, its feathers singed, lands on your arm. The seal is the Council's. The hand is shaking.
dialogue.sofe.act4.sulthari_besieged.3: "Sulthari is under siege. A spire of light hangs over the Observatory and the walls are failing. Come home, Bearer. Come home now."

item.sofe.ashbringer_of_the_first_fallen: Hits set the target ablaze (4 s). Hits wither the target (3 s). Each kill heals you 4.

message.sofe.nahrazel.sins: The seven sins wake in him at once
message.sofe.nahrazel.codex: You are inside the Codex. Break the seven Seals and rewrite it
message.sofe.nahrazel.rewritten: The seal is rewritten (%s of %s): strike him now!
message.sofe.nahrazel.fallen: The First Fallen falls. The Codex closes.
message.sofe.sin_power.lust: Lust: you are drawn to him
message.sofe.sin_power.envy: Envy: a copy of you rises
quest.sofe.act5_ascension.step1: Defeat Solrath in the Temple of Sulthari
quest.sofe.act5_ascension.step2: Climb the Celestial Spire and defeat Prython
quest.sofe.act5_ascension.step3: Cross the Void Gate and forge the Sealing Quill with Void Ink
dialogue.sofe.act5.the_siege.1: Sulthari burns. Over the Great Observatory a spire of white light hangs upside down from the sky, and the Void pours from its tip into the streets.
dialogue.sofe.act5.the_siege.2: Bearer! Ozhan sealed himself in the Temple when the walls broke. Since then the light has only grown. Go to him.
dialogue.sofe.act5.ozhan_unmasked.1: You came. Of course you came: you always do what you are told, Bearer. It is what I liked most about you.
dialogue.sofe.act5.ozhan_unmasked.2: Every fragment you won, I counted. Every Archsin you killed, I thanked. Prython promised me a seat above the Law, and I have taken it.
dialogue.sofe.act5.ozhan_unmasked.3: Kneel before Solrath. The Law was only ever a leash.
dialogue.sofe.act5.the_spire.1: With Solrath fallen, the light over the Observatory falters, and a stair opens in the Celestial Spire. It climbs into the sky, where Pride waits.
dialogue.sofe.act5.prython_temptation.1: Six of my brothers fell to you. Six! Do you understand what that makes you? Not a Bearer. A ruler.
dialogue.sofe.act5.prython_temptation.2: Look down. Every empire of Aetheris fits in your hand from here. Why give it back to the weak?
dialogue.sofe.act5.prythons_offer.1: Enough. Hand me the six fragments, and I will crown you over all of Aetheris. No Council. No Law. Only you.
dialogue.sofe.act5.the_inverted_throne.1: Prython falls, and the Spire falls with him: it turns over in the sky and sinks, point first, through the city and into the earth.
dialogue.sofe.act5.the_inverted_throne.2: Where it went down, a stair winds into the dark. At the bottom is the Inverted Throne, and on it, the one the Codex was made to hold.
dialogue.sofe.act5.the_first_fallen.1: Seven fragments. You carried every one of them to my door. Thank you, Bearer.

message.sofe.jeweler.how: Sockets %s/%s. Sneak to open one; hold a cut gem in the other hand to set it.
message.sofe.jeweler.rough: A rough gem must be cut first (use the bench with empty hands).
message.sofe.jeweler.no_socket: There is no open socket for it.
message.sofe.anvil.rerolled: The weakest affix is forged anew.
message.sofe.anvil.how: Hold a piece of SoFE gear: use to temper an affix (1 aetherium), sneak to reroll the weakest (2).
message.sofe.anvil.nothing: Nothing on this piece can be worked (Relics and gems are left alone).
message.sofe.anvil.worn_out: This piece has been tempered %s times already.
message.sofe.gate.void_gate: The Void Gate stays sealed until Envyris, the last Archsin of Aureum, has fallen.
message.sofe.camp.not_free: This camp still lives in fear: it trades once its Archsin has fallen.
dialogue.sofe.kerem.1: Every stone in Aetheris hides the face of a sin. Bring them to me rough; I will show you which.
dialogue.sofe.kerem.2: At my bench I cut them, open your steel and set them. Sneak at the bench to open a socket; hold the gem to set it.
dialogue.sofe.nilufar.1: The Void leaves a black residue in all it touches. Burnt clean, it is aetherium again: the Seal's own light.
dialogue.sofe.nilufar.2: Bring me the black shards and some coal. The Purifier does the rest; the Codex forgives what it can.
dialogue.sofe.zahir.1: Zahir the Wanderer, at your service. My caravan never stays: three days here, then wherever the road is free.
dialogue.sofe.zahir.2: What I carry, no city sells. One of each to each Bearer; the rest is for the next camp.
dialogue.sofe.camp.ferid: Ferid sent me with what he could spare. Now that the road is free, the camp breathes again.
dialogue.sofe.camp.dilara: Dilara's anvil travels with me. Bring me ingots and I will keep your steel sharp out here.
message.sofe.zahir.arrives: The caravan of Zahir the Wanderer has stopped at the %s, for three days.
Go back to whoever asked for your help in the Silk Wells camp.
The courtiers in the gardens are not dead, Bearer. They are dreaming the dream Luxara gave them: no hunger, no age, no end.
Her dancers guard them. Break the dancers, and then we must decide whether to wake them.
I will go to the gardens.
The gardens, far to the north-east. The dancers do not sleep.
The dancers are gone. The courtiers are still smiling in their sleep. Woken, they will remember everything they lost.
Do we wake them, and let Parsivan grieve and rebuild? Or let them dream, happy, until the dream ends by itself?
Wake them. A true life is worth its pain.
Then I will sit by each one as they open their eyes. Someone should be there.
Let them dream. They have suffered enough.
Then I will keep the roses for them. A garden for sleepers. Perhaps that is mercy.
quest.sofe.side.parsivan_silk_caravan.st: Go to the caravanserai on the Silk Road.
Go back to whoever asked for your help in the Silk Wells camp.
dialogue.sofe.q.parsivan_silk_caravan.of: The last caravan of moonsilk never reached the camp. The Void beasts stalk the caravanserai where it stopped.
Bring back what you can. We need cloth for the wounded, and something beautiful to remember who we were.
dialogue.sofe.q.parsivan_silk_caravan.ac: I will bring the silk home.
dialogue.sofe.q.parsivan_silk_caravan.re: The caravanserai on the Silk Road, east of the Baths.
dialogue.sofe.q.parsivan_silk_caravan.do: Moonsilk! It still shines. Look at it, catching the light like nothing happened.
Keep a share. Silk like this deserves to be worn by someone who fought for it.
quest.sofe.side.khemet_souls_below.step1: Go to the Catacombs of Khemet.
quest.sofe.side.khemet_souls_below.step3: Go back to whoever asked for your help in the Reed Shore camp.
dialogue.sofe.q.khemet_souls_below.offer: Down in the catacombs, the souls of the old kings sit in the dark with their eyes open. Morthis's mummies keep them there.
Clear the mummies. Then we must choose what those souls become.
dialogue.sofe.q.khemet_souls_below.accep: Take me to the river's end.
dialogue.sofe.q.khemet_souls_below.remin: The catacombs, south of the river. The kings are waiting.
dialogue.sofe.q.khemet_souls_below.choic: The mummies are dust. The kings still wait, and the river is ready to carry them. Or they could stay, and stand guard.
Do we guide them across, to rest at last? Or bind them to the tombs, to guard the living against what comes next?
dialogue.sofe.q.khemet_souls_below.answe: Guide them across. They have waited enough.
dialogue.sofe.q.khemet_souls_below.reply: Then my oar is wet again. I will row until the last king is home.
dialogue.sofe.q.khemet_souls_below.answe: Bind them. Khemet needs its kings to watch over it.
dialogue.sofe.q.khemet_souls_below.reply: Then the tombs will never be robbed again. But I will never row them home.
quest.sofe.side.khemet_sunken_archive.st: Go back to whoever asked for your help in the Reed Shore camp.
dialogue.sofe.q.khemet_sunken_archive.of: The archive of Khemet sank into the marsh, with every name, every law, every recipe for embalming the dead.
The Void wretches nest in its ruins. Clear them, and I will dive for whatever papyrus survived.
dialogue.sofe.q.khemet_sunken_archive.re: The Stagnant Marsh, far to the south-east.
dialogue.sofe.q.khemet_sunken_archive.do: Wet, blurred, but readable. The laws of the House of Thresholds, in my teacher's hand.
Take this papyrus. Whatever you write on it will last; sunreed does not forget.
quest.sofe.side.aureum_gold_of_the_court: Go to the Treasury of Aureum.
Go back to whoever asked for your help in the Broken Aqueduct camp.
dialogue.sofe.q.aureum_gold_of_the_court: The Treasury still holds the gold that bought every judge in Aureum. Goldarc's legionnaires guard it as if it were sacred.
Break the guard. Then the gold is ours, and we must decide what it is for.
Let us see this sacred gold.
The Treasury, west of Sulthari, over the border.
The gold is free. Enough to rebuild the courts with honest judges and walls no coin can climb. Or enough to feed every family in Aureum for years.
Do we restore the Law, slowly and properly? Or give the gold back to the people it was stolen from?
Then I will sit in the Senate again, and this time I will not be for sale.
Give it back to the people.
Then tonight every hearth in Aureum will be warm. The Senate can wait. Bellies cannot.
quest.sofe.side.aureum_bread_and_circuse: Go back to whoever asked for your help in the Broken Aqueduct camp.
dialogue.sofe.q.aureum_bread_and_circuse: The shades of the crowd make the dead fight on in the Colosseum: gladiators who never got to retire.
My brothers are down there. Give them a last fight worth losing.
They will have their last fight.
The Colosseum, far to the south-west.
The stands are quiet. My brothers are quiet. For the first time, the Colosseum sounds like a grave and not a market.
This orichalcum was the prize they never claimed. Forge something that protects, not something that entertains.
quest.sofe.bearer.cassian_act3.step3: Go back to whoever asked for your help in the Silk Wells camp.
dialogue.sofe.q.cassian_act3.offer.1: A knight of your Order came to the Moonlit Baths the night your brothers were tried. He never left.
dialogue.sofe.q.cassian_act3.offer.2: They say his signet still gleams on the bottom of the pool, under the Void things that drink there.
dialogue.sofe.q.cassian_act3.accept: Then I will bring him home.
dialogue.sofe.q.cassian_act3.reminder: The Baths, west of the camp. The signet is waiting.
dialogue.sofe.q.cassian_act3.done.1: His signet. And a letter: 'The judges were paid in Aureum gold. I go to warn the Order. If I fall, carry the Scale.'
dialogue.sofe.q.cassian_act3.done.2: He did not reach them. But you did. Wear it.
quest.sofe.bearer.cassian_act4.step1: Go to the Treasury of Aureum.
quest.sofe.bearer.cassian_act4.step3: Go back to whoever asked for your help in the Broken Aqueduct camp.
dialogue.sofe.q.cassian_act4.offer.1: Knight, I have read the Treasury ledgers. Your Order's trial was paid for in one entry: thirty talents, 'for the Scale'.
dialogue.sofe.q.cassian_act4.offer.2: The coins are still in the Treasury vaults, guarded. Take them back, and let the Senate see what it sold.
dialogue.sofe.q.cassian_act4.accept: Thirty talents. My brothers were worth more.
dialogue.sofe.q.cassian_act4.reminder: The Treasury. Thirty talents, and your brothers' names.
dialogue.sofe.q.cassian_act4.done.1: The Senate read the ledger aloud. Nobody spoke for a long time. Then they voted to clear the Order's name.
dialogue.sofe.q.cassian_act4.done.2: Among the coins was this helm, pawned by the last knight to stand trial. It is yours now. The last knight is you.
quest.sofe.bearer.ankhareth_act3.step1: Go to the Catacombs of Khemet.
quest.sofe.bearer.ankhareth_act3.step3: Go back to whoever asked for your help in the Reed Shore camp.
dialogue.sofe.q.ankhareth_act3.offer.1: Ankhareth. Your teacher lies in the catacombs, unwrapped. Morthis's mummies took her bandages for themselves.
dialogue.sofe.q.ankhareth_act3.offer.2: Only an embalmer of the House may wrap her again. That is you. That was always going to be you.
dialogue.sofe.q.ankhareth_act3.accept: I will wrap her as she wrapped others.
dialogue.sofe.q.ankhareth_act3.reminder: The catacombs. She is waiting, uncovered.
dialogue.sofe.q.ankhareth_act3.done.1: You wrapped her. I saw your hands shake, and then stop shaking. That is how she taught you.
dialogue.sofe.q.ankhareth_act3.done.2: She wore this ring to the end. It holds the souls she could not guide. Guide them for her.
quest.sofe.bearer.ankhareth_act4.step3: Go back to whoever asked for your help in the Broken Aqueduct camp.
dialogue.sofe.q.ankhareth_act4.offer.1: Priest of Khemet. In Aureum we never buried our gladiators. We dragged them out and sold the sand.
dialogue.sofe.q.ankhareth_act4.offer.2: Their shades are in the Colosseum. They have never had a funeral. Can you give them one?
dialogue.sofe.q.ankhareth_act4.accept: Every soul deserves its crossing. Even here.
dialogue.sofe.q.ankhareth_act4.reminder: The Colosseum. The shades have waited centuries.
dialogue.sofe.q.ankhareth_act4.done.1: You said their names, the ones the crowd never learned. I heard the stands go silent for the first time.
dialogue.sofe.q.ankhareth_act4.done.2: A ferryman's mask was found in the arena's cellar. Someone from Khemet came here before you. Wear it.
quest.sofe.bearer.shirin_act3.step3: Go back to whoever asked for your help in the Silk Wells camp.
dialogue.sofe.q.shirin_act3.offer.1: Lady Shirin. Your sister sleeps by the great fountain in the gardens. Luxara keeps her closest of all.
dialogue.sofe.q.shirin_act3.offer.2: The dancers will not let anyone near her. Except, perhaps, someone she would want to see.
dialogue.sofe.q.shirin_act3.reminder: The gardens. She is by the fountain.
dialogue.sofe.q.shirin_act3.done.1: You reached her. She did not wake, but she smiled when you said her name, a real smile.
dialogue.sofe.q.shirin_act3.done.2: She held this ring in her fist. Three runes: the ones you learned together. She was waiting for you.
quest.sofe.bearer.shirin_act4.step3: Go back to whoever asked for your help in the Broken Aqueduct camp.
dialogue.sofe.q.shirin_act4.offer.1: A veil of Parsivan silk is for sale in the Forum Market, with a price no one can pay. The merchant says it belonged to a sorceress.
dialogue.sofe.q.shirin_act4.offer.2: The Void beasts own the market now. Nobody is selling anything. Go and take it.
dialogue.sofe.q.shirin_act4.accept: It is hers. I know it.
dialogue.sofe.q.shirin_act4.reminder: The Forum Market, west of the camp.
dialogue.sofe.q.shirin_act4.done.1: It smells of jasmine and ink. Laleh's smell, you say? Then she passed through Aureum, before the gardens.
dialogue.sofe.q.shirin_act4.done.2: Wear it. Whatever she was running from, she left this behind so you could follow.
quest.sofe.bearer.rurik_act3: The Guild of the Silk Road
quest.sofe.bearer.rurik_act3.step1: Go to the caravanserai on the Silk Road.
quest.sofe.bearer.rurik_act3.step3: Go back to whoever asked for your help in the Silk Wells camp.
dialogue.sofe.q.rurik_act3.offer.1: Grimsson, isn't it? The thieves of the Silk Road spoke of a northern boy who robbed them once and lived.
dialogue.sofe.q.rurik_act3.offer.2: Their guildhouse is in the caravanserai, overrun. They kept records of every fence. Every one. Even the one who sold your clan.
dialogue.sofe.q.rurik_act3.reminder: The caravanserai. The guild's books are in the cellar.
dialogue.sofe.q.rurik_act3.done.1: The book says your clan's goods went west, to a fence in Aureum's market. A hooded merchant with no face.
dialogue.sofe.q.rurik_act3.done.2: And the guild left this hood. Ash-grey. They say it was made for the best thief they ever failed to catch.
quest.sofe.bearer.rurik_act4.step3: Go back to whoever asked for your help in the Broken Aqueduct camp.
dialogue.sofe.q.rurik_act4.offer.1: The faceless merchant's stock went to the Golden Vaults when Avarok took them. Everything stolen in Aureum ends there.
dialogue.sofe.q.rurik_act4.offer.2: If anything of your village survived, it is in those vaults.
dialogue.sofe.q.rurik_act4.accept: Then I'm robbing the greediest vault in the world.
dialogue.sofe.q.rurik_act4.reminder: The Golden Vaults, far to the west.
dialogue.sofe.q.rurik_act4.done.1: A pair of boots, sealskin, stitched with your clan's knot. Your mother's work, you said?
dialogue.sofe.q.rurik_act4.done.2: Then they are the only thing in those vaults that was never stolen. They were waiting to be returned.
quest.sofe.bearer.azhar_act3.step1: Go to the Catacombs of Khemet.
quest.sofe.bearer.azhar_act3.step3: Go back to whoever asked for your help in the Reed Shore camp.
dialogue.sofe.q.azhar_act3.offer.1: Majesty. Your ancestor Tevfiran signed a treaty with the kings of Khemet, sealed in their catacombs. Nobody has read it since.
dialogue.sofe.q.azhar_act3.offer.2: If Sulthari still honours it, Khemet will stand with you. If not, you should know what was promised.
dialogue.sofe.q.azhar_act3.accept: A sultan should know his debts.
dialogue.sofe.q.azhar_act3.reminder: The catacombs. The treaty lies with the kings.
dialogue.sofe.q.azhar_act3.done.1: The treaty promises that Sulthari would come when Khemet called. Khemet called, Majesty. For a hundred years.
dialogue.sofe.q.azhar_act3.done.2: You came. Late, but you came. Tevfiran's signet was sealed with the treaty. It is yours to keep the promise.
quest.sofe.bearer.azhar_act4.step3: Go back to whoever asked for your help in the Broken Aqueduct camp.
dialogue.sofe.q.azhar_act4.offer.1: A Republic does not kneel to sultans. But it remembers who stood in its market when the legionnaires turned on the people.
dialogue.sofe.q.azhar_act4.offer.2: Go to the Forum. Stand there. Let them see you.
dialogue.sofe.q.azhar_act4.reminder: The Forum Market. Aureum is watching.
dialogue.sofe.q.azhar_act4.done.1: The Senate sent this: the turban of the Peacock Throne, taken from your grandfather's embassy in a bad year.
dialogue.sofe.q.azhar_act4.done.2: They say it is not a gift. It is a return. Republics, Majesty, are very particular about the difference.
dialogue.sofe.cassian.act3: Luxara offered me a court where no one is ever betrayed. I almost said yes.
dialogue.sofe.cassian.act4: Aureum paid for my brothers' deaths. I came here to judge it, and found widows instead.
dialogue.sofe.ankhareth.act3: Khemet is home, and home is asleep. I keep wanting to lie down beside it.
dialogue.sofe.ankhareth.act4: In Aureum the dead are counted like coins. I count them like people.
dialogue.sofe.shirin.act3: Laleh is in those gardens. If Luxara offers me her, whole and happy, I do not know what I will say.
dialogue.sofe.shirin.act4: She passed through here before me. I keep finding her handwriting in the margins of other people's books.
dialogue.sofe.rurik.act3: Silk Road thieves have long memories. Mine is longer.
dialogue.sofe.rurik.act4: Aureum has more locks than any city alive. I have never felt more at home.
dialogue.sofe.azhar.act3: Khemet called to Sulthari for a hundred years. We had stopped listening.
dialogue.sofe.azhar.act4: A Republic does not need a king. Perhaps that is the lesson Sulthari needs.
dialogue.sofe.parsivan_poet.act1.1: Luxara's court still sings in the gardens. Every song is sweeter than the last, and every singer thinner.
dialogue.sofe.parsivan_poet.act1.2: I fled with a single verse in my head: the one she could not make me forget. I will write it down when we are free.
dialogue.sofe.parsivan_poet.act4.1: The verse I kept? It says: 'Desire is a door, not a home.' I wrote it on the camp's first wall.
dialogue.sofe.parsivan_gardener.act1.1: I tended the queen's roses for thirty years. Now they bloom at midnight and smell of honey and blood.
dialogue.sofe.parsivan_gardener.act1.2: The courtiers lie among them, smiling, and do not wake. Some of them were my friends.
dialogue.sofe.parsivan_gardener.act4.1: The roses bloom by day again. Ordinary roses. I never thought I would cry over ordinary roses.
dialogue.sofe.parsivan_dancer.act1.1: The mirage dancers wear our faces. Mine is out there somewhere, still dancing for her.
dialogue.sofe.parsivan_dancer.act1.2: If you meet a dancer who looks like me, do not hesitate. She is not me. I am here.
dialogue.sofe.parsivan_dancer.act4.1: I danced last night, for nobody, for myself. It is the first dance that belonged to me in years.
dialogue.sofe.khemet_embalmer.act1.1: The dead of Khemet are not resting, they are waiting. Morthis taught them that nothing is worth getting up for.
dialogue.sofe.khemet_embalmer.act1.2: We still wrap them, out of habit. Habit is all that is left of the House of Thresholds.
dialogue.sofe.khemet_embalmer.act4.1: The jars are singing again, the old way. The dead have somewhere to go.
dialogue.sofe.khemet_ferryman.act1.1: I rowed the dead across the river for forty years. Now the river does not move, and neither do they.
dialogue.sofe.khemet_ferryman.act1.2: My oar is dry. A ferryman with a dry oar is a man with nothing to do but remember.
dialogue.sofe.khemet_ferryman.act4.1: The river woke up this morning. I nearly lost my hat. I have never been so happy to nearly lose a hat.
dialogue.sofe.khemet_scribe.act1.1: I copy the names of the dead onto sunreed papyrus, so someone remembers them. The list grows faster than my reed.
dialogue.sofe.khemet_scribe.act1.2: The old archive lies under the marsh now. Everything we were, rotting slowly, the way Morthis likes it.
dialogue.sofe.khemet_scribe.act4.1: I am writing a new list: the names of those who came home. It is shorter. But it is growing.
dialogue.sofe.aureum_senator.act1.1: The Republic had laws for everything, Bearer, except for a Senate that could be bought. Envyris did not need to buy us. We sold ourselves.
dialogue.sofe.aureum_senator.act1.2: I kept my toga and lost my vote. Here in the camp, at least, nobody pretends otherwise.
dialogue.sofe.aureum_senator.act5.1: They are talking about elections in the camp. Elections! I had forgotten the word tasted like that.
dialogue.sofe.aureum_gladiator.act1.1: I won forty fights in the Colosseum. The crowd that cheered me now sits in the stands as shades, and still cheers.
dialogue.sofe.aureum_gladiator.act1.2: They want blood more than they want bread. Envy turns spectators into wolves.
dialogue.sofe.aureum_gladiator.act5.1: The sand of the arena is just sand now. I took a handful. I do not know why. Maybe to remember I left alive.
dialogue.sofe.aureum_widow.act1.1: My husband minted coins for the Treasury. They took him for a coin he did not strike. Gold has a long memory and no mercy.
dialogue.sofe.aureum_widow.act1.2: Everyone in Aureum envies someone. I envy the dead. They no longer count anything.
dialogue.sofe.aureum_widow.act5.1: I bought bread today with a coin and the baker gave me change without counting it twice. Aureum is healing.
dialogue.sofe.parsivan_poet.fate.awakene: The court is awake, and weeping, and arguing, and alive. I have never heard anything so beautiful.
dialogue.sofe.parsivan_poet.fate.asleep: The gardens are silent and full of smiles. Sometimes I go and read my verse to the sleepers. Nobody answers.
dialogue.sofe.khemet_embalmer.fate.rest: Every jar sings, every boat sails. Khemet is a land of the dead again, and so, at last, of the living.
dialogue.sofe.khemet_embalmer.fate.guard: The kings stand at the tomb doors with their eyes open. The robbers have stopped coming. So have the mourners.
dialogue.sofe.aureum_widow.fate.law: The courts open tomorrow. My husband's case will be the first. They say the judge cannot be bought. We shall see.
dialogue.sofe.aureum_widow.fate.shared: There is bread on every table and gold in every hand. Nobody envies anybody this week. It will not last, but it is sweet.
message.sofe.coffer.waiting: Your Reward Coffer waits in the arena. It fades in thirty minutes if it is not opened.
message.sofe.coffer.faded: Your unopened Reward Coffer has faded away.
message.sofe.soulbound.full: Your pack is full: it lies at your feet, and only you can take it.
message.sofe.death.title: You have died
message.sofe.death.countdown: Watching the fight... you return in %s s
dialogue.sofe.isfaran_perfumer.act1.1: Every perfume I make smells of her now: honey, roses, something sweeter underneath. I cannot make it stop.
dialogue.sofe.isfaran_perfumer.act1.2: If a scent makes you forget why you came, Bearer, walk the other way.
dialogue.sofe.isfaran_perfumer.act4.1: I made a perfume of rain and ink this morning. Nobody wanted it more than me.
dialogue.sofe.isfaran_guard.act1.1: I keep the gate, but half the court never comes out of the gardens. I am guarding an empty city.
dialogue.sofe.isfaran_guard.act1.2: The ones who leave smile at me as if I were a dream. I am not. I am cold and my feet hurt.
dialogue.sofe.isfaran_guard.act4.1: People come through the gate again, arguing about prices. I have never loved arguing so much.
dialogue.sofe.isfaran_astronomer.act1.1: The stars over Isfaran have stopped moving in my charts. Either the sky is asleep, or I am.
dialogue.sofe.isfaran_astronomer.act1.2: Laleh of the Observatory came here once. She said the gardens were a door, and someone left it open.
dialogue.sofe.isfaran_astronomer.act4.1: The sky turns again. I wept over a chart, and the ink ran into a new constellation.
dialogue.sofe.isfaran_child.act1.1: My mother sleeps in the garden and won't come home. She says it's nicer there. It isn't. I checked.
dialogue.sofe.isfaran_child.act1.2: Are you the one who wakes people up? Can you wake her first?
dialogue.sofe.isfaran_child.act4.1: Mama is home! She burned the rice. It was the best rice ever.
dialogue.sofe.isfaran_carpet_weaver.act1: My carpets used to tell stories. Now every pattern I weave turns into the same face.
Bring me moonsilk, if the caravans ever run again. I want to weave something that is mine.
dialogue.sofe.isfaran_carpet_weaver.act4: The new carpet tells your story, Bearer. I left a knot loose at the end. Stories should not be finished.
dialogue.sofe.neferet_priest.act1.1: We say the morning prayers to an empty sky. The sun still rises; it simply does not seem to care.
dialogue.sofe.neferet_priest.act1.2: Morthis sleeps on a throne in the marsh, and all of Khemet yawns with him.
dialogue.sofe.neferet_priest.act4.1: The temple was full at dawn. People came to pray and stayed to work. That is the best prayer.
dialogue.sofe.neferet_boatman.act1.1: The canal barely moves. My boat sits in it like a fly in honey.
dialogue.sofe.neferet_boatman.act1.2: My cousin Ani rows the dead. I row the living. Lately our passengers look the same.
dialogue.sofe.neferet_boatman.act4.1: The water runs! I nearly fell in. Tell Ani the river remembers how to be a river.
dialogue.sofe.neferet_potter.act1.1: I have not finished a jar in a month. I sit at the wheel and watch it turn, and that seems like enough.
dialogue.sofe.neferet_potter.act1.2: That is the sin, Bearer. It never feels like a sin. It feels like rest.
dialogue.sofe.neferet_potter.act4.1: Twelve jars since yesterday! My hands hurt. I had forgotten that hurting hands are happy hands.
dialogue.sofe.neferet_child.act1.1: I climbed the small pyramid. From the top you can see the marsh. It looks like a sleeping animal.
dialogue.sofe.neferet_child.act1.2: My grandpa says the kings are awake under the sand, waiting. I don't think waiting is fun.
dialogue.sofe.neferet_child.act4.1: The marsh doesn't look like an animal anymore. Just a marsh. A bit smelly. I like it better.
dialogue.sofe.neferet_guard.act1.1: The mummies of the marsh walk to our walls at night and stop, as if they forgot why they came.
dialogue.sofe.neferet_guard.act1.2: I do not know if that is a mercy or a warning.
dialogue.sofe.neferet_guard.act4.1: No mummies last night. I slept, and I did not feel guilty about it. That is how I knew it was over.
dialogue.sofe.aurelion_magistrate.act1.1: I judge cases where both sides envy each other so much that neither wants to win, only to see the other lose.
dialogue.sofe.aurelion_magistrate.act1.2: The law was written for greed. Nobody wrote one for envy.
dialogue.sofe.aurelion_magistrate.act5.1: A man thanked his neighbour in my court today. I adjourned for an hour to recover.
dialogue.sofe.aurelion_legionary.act1.1: My cohort was sent to guard the Treasury. Half of them never came back. The other half came back gilded.
dialogue.sofe.aurelion_legionary.act1.2: If you see a golden legionary, Bearer, do not look him in the eye. It was one of us.
dialogue.sofe.aurelion_legionary.act5.1: I marched past the Treasury today. Only stone and coins. I saluted anyway.
dialogue.sofe.aurelion_baker.act1.1: People buy bread only to see if their neighbour's loaf is bigger. I bake them all the same, and still they quarrel.
dialogue.sofe.aurelion_baker.act1.2: Envy is a hunger bread does not fill.
dialogue.sofe.aurelion_baker.act5.1: Today two customers shared a loaf. Shared! I gave them a second one for free.
dialogue.sofe.aurelion_child.act1.1: I wanted to be a gladiator. Now the gladiators are shadows. I want to be a baker.
dialogue.sofe.aurelion_child.act1.2: Bakers don't turn into shadows, right?
dialogue.sofe.aurelion_child.act5.1: I'm going to be a baker AND a gladiator. A gladiator who bakes. Nobody has thought of that.
dialogue.sofe.aurelion_sculptor.act1.1: They paid me to carve the Senate's faces in gold. Every statue I finish, someone pays me to make the next one taller.
dialogue.sofe.aurelion_sculptor.act1.2: I am carving a very small statue now, of my daughter. Nobody will envy it. That is the point.
dialogue.sofe.aurelion_sculptor.act5.1: The Senate asked for a statue of you, Bearer. I said I would carve it life-sized, no taller. They agreed!

quest.sofe.act5_ascension.step4: Descend to the Inverted Throne and defeat Nahrazel
dialogue.sofe.act5.the_sealing_quill.1: The stair will not open for you, Bearer. A seal is a page, and his was written from the other side.
dialogue.sofe.act5.the_sealing_quill.2: Go through the Void Gate, into the Outer Void. Bring back its crystal, and the ink the Alembic draws from it.
dialogue.sofe.act5.the_sealing_quill.3: A feather, the ink, a crystal of the Void and a shard of clean aetherium: that is the Sealing Quill. Only with it will the Throne let you down.
dialogue.sofe.act5.the_quill_forged.1: The Quill drinks the Void Ink, and its nib glows like the edge of a page about to burn. Beneath Sulthari, the stair to the Inverted Throne lies open.
scene.sofe.crowned_in_ash.knight.1: The Order of the Scale kneels before you. You melted its scales into your crown.
scene.sofe.crowned_in_ash.knight.2: The courts of Aureum judge in your name now, and every sentence is the same.
scene.sofe.crowned_in_ash.knight.3: Your wrath is the only Law left, and no one has lived to break it.
scene.sofe.crowned_in_ash.knight.4: Cassian sits on a throne of ash, and the scale in his hand weighs nothing at all.
scene.sofe.crowned_in_ash.necromancer.1: The gates of the underworld stand open, and no soul is allowed through them.
scene.sofe.crowned_in_ash.necromancer.2: The dead of Khemet stand in rows forever, guarding a king who never walks.
scene.sofe.crowned_in_ash.necromancer.3: Among them is your master, still waiting for the journey you promised him.
scene.sofe.crowned_in_ash.necromancer.4: Ankhareth rules the dead of Aetheris, and none of them will ever rest.
scene.sofe.crowned_in_ash.sorceress.1: The stars of Parsivan burn out one by one, until only your light is left in the sky.
scene.sofe.crowned_in_ash.sorceress.2: The court dreams of you now, and only of you.
scene.sofe.crowned_in_ash.sorceress.3: Laleh's voice still calls from the Gardens. You stopped listening long ago.
scene.sofe.crowned_in_ash.sorceress.4: Shirin draws the new map of the sky, and her sister's name is not on it.
scene.sofe.crowned_in_ash.thief.1: All the gold of Aetheris fills your vaults. The Nordrath clans dig it for you, in chains.
scene.sofe.crowned_in_ash.thief.2: Your village was never rebuilt. There was no profit in it.
scene.sofe.crowned_in_ash.thief.3: You count your coins every night, and every night one is missing.
scene.sofe.crowned_in_ash.thief.4: Rurik owns everything, and keeps nothing worth keeping.
scene.sofe.crowned_in_ash.king.1: Emperor of Aetheris. Every crown of every empire was melted into yours.
scene.sofe.crowned_in_ash.king.2: There is no Council now, and no Pact: only your word, carved in every square.
scene.sofe.crowned_in_ash.king.3: Sulthari kneels in the ash of its own Observatory, and calls it glory.
scene.sofe.crowned_in_ash.king.4: Azhar sits beneath the false sun, and the Codex beneath his throne lies open.
scene.sofe.crowned_in_ash.title: Crowned in Ash
scene.sofe.crowned_in_ash.wake: You blink. The wind on the Spire. Prython's hand is still held out to you.
advancement.sofe.crowned_in_ash.desc: Wear Pride's crown, for a moment.
item.sofe.sealing_quill.desc: Ink from the other side of the seal. It opens the Inverted Throne.
